verses.16:29: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls and do no work at all, whether the native-born or the stranger who sojourns in your midst.
verses.16:30: For on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins you shall be clean before the LORD.
verses.16:31: It is a Sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall afflict your souls; it is a perpetual statute.
verses.16:32: And the priest who is anointed and consecrated to minister as priest in place of his father shall make atonement, and shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments.
verses.16:33: He shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make atonement for the tent of meeting and for the altar; and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
verses.16:34: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you, to make atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year." And he did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.17:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.17:2: "Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them, 'This is the thing which the LORD has commanded, saying:
verses.17:3: "Any man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or a lamb or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,
verses.17:4: and has not brought it to the doorway of the tent of meeting to present an offering to the LORD before the tabernacle of the LORD, bloodguilt shall be reckoned to that man—he has shed blood—and that man shall be cut off from the midst of his people;
verses.17:5: so that the children of Israel may bring their sacrifices which they sacrifice in the open field, and bring them to the LORD, to the doorway of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as peace offerings to the LORD.
verses.17:6: And the priest shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar of the LORD at the doorway of the tent of meeting, and burn the fat as a soothing aroma to the LORD.
verses.17:7: And they shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat demons, after whom they play the harlot. This shall be a perpetual statute to them throughout their generations."'
verses.17:8: And you shall say to them, 'Any man of the house of Israel, or of the sojourner who sojourns in their midst, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
verses.17:9: and does not bring it to the doorway of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, that man shall be cut off from his people.
verses.17:10: And any man of the house of Israel, or of the sojourner who sojourns in their midst, who eats any blood, I will set My face against the soul who eats blood, and I will cut him off from the midst of his people.
verses.17:11: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls; for the blood itself makes atonement by the life.
verses.17:12: Therefore I have said to the children of Israel, "No soul among you shall eat blood, nor shall the sojourner who sojourns in your midst eat blood."
verses.17:13: And any man of the children of Israel, or of the sojourner who sojourns in their midst, who hunts and catches any wild beast or bird that may be eaten, shall pour out its blood and cover it with dust.
verses.17:14: For as for the life of all flesh, its blood is one with its life; therefore I said to the children of Israel, "You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it shall be cut off."
verses.17:15: And every soul who eats that which dies of itself, or that which is torn by beasts, whether native-born or sojourner, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until the evening; then he shall be clean.
verses.17:16: But if he does not wash them nor bathe his flesh, then he shall bear his iniquity.'"
verses.18:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.18:2: "Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, 'I am the LORD your God.
verses.18:3: According to the deeds of the land of Egypt, where you dwelt, you shall not do; and according to the deeds of the land of Canaan, to which I am bringing you, you shall not do; nor shall you walk in their statutes.
verses.18:4: You shall perform My judgments and keep My statutes, to walk in them: I am the LORD your God.
verses.18:5: And you shall keep My statutes and My judgments; the man who does them shall live by them. I am the LORD.
verses.18:6: No man among you shall draw near to any close relative of his flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.
verses.18:7: The nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover; she is your mother—you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:8: The nakedness of the wife of your father you shall not uncover; it is the nakedness of your father.
verses.18:9: The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother, whether born at home or born outside—their nakedness you shall not uncover.
verses.18:10: The nakedness of the daughter of your son or of the daughter of your daughter—their nakedness you shall not uncover, for theirs is your own nakedness.
verses.18:11: The nakedness of the daughter of the wife of your father, born to your father—she is your sister—you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:12: The nakedness of the sister of your father you shall not uncover; she is the near kinswoman of your father.
verses.18:13: The nakedness of the sister of your mother you shall not uncover, for she is the near kinswoman of your mother.
verses.18:14: The nakedness of the brother of your father you shall not uncover; you shall not draw near to his wife—she is your aunt.
verses.18:15: The nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover; she is the wife of your son—you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:16: The nakedness of the wife of your brother you shall not uncover; it is the nakedness of your brother.
verses.18:17: The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover, nor shall you take the daughter of her son or the daughter of her daughter to uncover her nakedness; they are her near kinswomen; it is depravity.
verses.18:18: Nor shall you take a woman in addition to her sister, as a rival, to uncover her nakedness beside her during her lifetime.
verses.18:19: And you shall not draw near to a woman in her menstrual uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:20: And you shall not lie carnally with the wife of your neighbor, to defile yourself with her.
verses.18:21: And you shall not give any of your offspring to pass over to Molech, nor shall you profane the name of your God: I am the LORD.
verses.18:22: You shall not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination.
verses.18:23: Nor shall you lie with any beast to defile yourself with it; nor shall any woman stand before a beast to mate with it: it is perversion.
verses.18:24: Do not defile yourselves with any of these things; for by all these the nations are defiled, which I am driving out before you.
verses.18:25: And the land became defiled, so I visited its iniquity upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
verses.18:26: But you yourselves shall keep My statutes and My judgments, and shall not commit any of these abominations, neither the native-born nor the sojourner who sojourns in your midst,
verses.18:27: for all these abominations the men of the land who were before you committed, and the land became defiled,
verses.18:28: lest the land vomit you out when you defile it, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
verses.18:29: For whoever commits any of these abominations, the souls who commit them shall be cut off from the midst of their people.
verses.18:30: Therefore you shall keep My charge, so that you do not practice any of the abominable customs which were practiced before you, and that you do not defile yourselves by them: I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.19:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.19:2: "Speak to the entire congregation of the children of Israel, and say to them, 'You shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy.
verses.19:3: Each one of you shall revere his mother and his father, and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:4: Do not turn to idols, nor make for yourselves molten gods; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:5: And when you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
verses.19:6: It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it and on the next day; and whatever remains until the third day shall be burned with fire.
verses.19:7: And if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination; it shall not be accepted.
verses.19:8: Therefore whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the holy thing of the LORD; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
verses.19:9: When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap to the very edges of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
verses.19:10: You shall not strip your vineyard bare, nor shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:11: You shall not steal, nor deceive, nor lie one to another.
verses.19:12: And you shall not swear falsely by My name, and so profane the name of your God; I am the LORD.
verses.19:13: You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor rob him. The wages of a hired laborer shall not remain with you overnight until morning.
verses.19:14: You shall not curse the deaf, nor place a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God; I am the LORD.
verses.19:15: You shall commit no injustice in judgment; you shall neither show partiality to the poor nor defer to the mighty, but in righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.
verses.19:16: You shall not go about as a talebearer among your people, nor shall you stand against the blood of your neighbor; I am the LORD.
verses.19:17: You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely reprove your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
verses.19:18: You shall not avenge yourself, nor harbor a grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the LORD.
verses.19:19: You shall keep My statutes. You shall not breed your livestock with another kind; you shall not sow your field with mixed seed; nor shall a garment of mixed woven fabric come upon you.
verses.19:20: And if a man lies carnally with a woman who is a female servant designated for another man, and she has not been redeemed at all nor has freedom been granted to her, there shall be an inquiry; they shall not be put to death, because she was not freed.
verses.19:21: And he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tabernacle of meeting, a ram as a guilt offering.
verses.19:22: And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for the sin which he has committed, and he shall be forgiven for the sin which he has committed.
verses.19:23: And when you enter the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you shall regard its fruit as uncircumcised; for three years it shall be as uncircumcised to you, and it shall not be eaten.
verses.19:24: But in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a tribute of praise to the LORD.
verses.19:25: And in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that its yield may be increased for you; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:26: You shall not eat anything with its blood; you shall not practice divination, nor soothsaying.
verses.19:27: You shall not round off the hair at the sides of your head, nor shall you mar the edges of your beard.
verses.19:28: You shall not make any gashes in your flesh for the dead, nor imprint any tattoo marks upon yourselves; I am the LORD.
verses.19:29: Do not profane your daughter by making her a harlot, lest the land fall into harlotry and the land be filled with wickedness.
verses.19:30: You shall observe My Sabbaths and revere My sanctuary; I am the LORD.
verses.19:31: Do not turn to mediums or to spiritists; do not seek them out to be defiled by them; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:32: You shall rise before the gray-headed and honor the presence of an aged man, and fear your God; I am the LORD.
verses.19:33: And if a sojourner dwells with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.
verses.19:34: The sojourner who dwells with you shall be to you as one native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt; I am the LORD your God.
verses.19:35: You shall commit no injustice in judgment, in measurement of length, in weight, or in volume.
verses.19:36: Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin you shall have; I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.
verses.19:37: Therefore you shall keep all My statutes and all My judgments, and perform them; I am the LORD.'"
verses.20:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.20:2: "Moreover, you shall say to the children of Israel, 'Any man of the children of Israel, or of the sojourners who dwell in Israel, who gives any of his offspring to Molech, shall surely be put to death; the people of the land shall stone him with stones.
verses.20:3: And I Myself will set My face against that man and cut him off from the midst of his people, because he has given of his offspring to Molech, defiling My sanctuary and profaning My holy name.
verses.20:4: And if the people of the land indeed hide their eyes from that man when he gives of his offspring to Molech, and do not put him to death,
verses.20:5: then I Myself will set My face against that man and against his family, and I will cut off him and all who turn after him to play the harlot after Molech from the midst of their people.
verses.20:6: And as for the soul who turns to mediums and to spiritists, to play the harlot after them, I will set My face against that soul and cut him off from the midst of his people.
verses.20:7: Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.20:8: And you shall observe My statutes and perform them; I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
verses.20:9: For anyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother; his blood shall be upon him.
verses.20:10: And the man who commits adultery with another man's wife, even he who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife—the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
verses.20:11: The man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness; both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.
verses.20:12: And if a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall surely be put to death. They have committed perversion; their blood shall be upon them.
verses.20:13: And if a man lies with a male as with a woman, both of them have done an abomination; they shall surely be put to death, and their blood shall be upon them.
verses.20:14: And if a man takes a woman and her mother, it is depravity; they shall burn both him and them with fire, so that there may be no depravity in your midst.
verses.20:15: And if a man lies with a beast, he shall surely be put to death, and you shall slay the beast.
verses.20:16: And if a woman approaches any beast to mate with it, you shall slay both the woman and the beast; they shall surely be put to death, and their blood shall be upon them.
verses.20:17: And if a man takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace; and they shall be cut off in the sight of the children of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity.
verses.20:18: And if a man lies with a woman during her monthly impurity and uncovers her nakedness, he has laid bare her fountain, and she has uncovered the fountain of her blood; both of them shall be cut off from the midst of their people.
verses.20:19: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister nor of your father's sister, for whoever does so lays bare his own near kin; they shall bear their iniquity.
verses.20:20: And if a man lies with his uncle's wife, he has uncovered his uncle's nakedness; they shall bear their sin, and they shall die childless.
verses.20:21: And if a man takes his brother's wife, it is an impure thing; he has uncovered his brother's nakedness, and they shall be childless.
verses.20:22: You shall therefore observe all My statutes and all My judgments, and perform them, lest the land into which I am bringing you to dwell vomit you out.
verses.20:23: And you shall not walk in the customs of the nation which I am driving out before you, for they practiced all these things, and I abhorred them.
verses.20:24: But I have said to you, "You shall inherit their land, and I Myself will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey." I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.
verses.20:25: You shall therefore distinguish between the clean beast and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean; and you shall not make your souls detestable by beast, or by bird, or by anything that creeps upon the ground, which I have separated for you to regard as unclean.
verses.20:26: Thus you shall be holy to Me, for I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the peoples so that you should belong to Me.
verses.20:27: And a man or a woman in whom there is a spirit of a medium or a spiritist shall surely be put to death; they shall stone them with stones, and their blood shall be upon them.'"
verses.21:1: And the LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and declare to them, 'None of them shall defile himself for a dead body among his people,
verses.21:2: except for his blood relative who is nearest to him: for his mother, for his father, for his son, for his daughter, and for his brother;
verses.21:3: and for his virgin sister who is near to him, who has not belonged to a husband—for her he may defile himself.
verses.21:4: He shall not defile himself as a husband among his people, so as to profane himself.
verses.21:5: They shall not make any bald patch upon their head, nor shave off the edges of their beard, nor cut any gashes in their flesh.
verses.21:6: They shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for they present the fire offerings of the LORD, the bread of their God; therefore they shall be holy.
verses.21:7: They shall not take in marriage a woman who is a harlot or one who has been defiled, nor shall they take a woman divorced from her husband, for he is holy to his God.
verses.21:8: Therefore you shall regard him as holy, for he offers the bread of your God; he shall be holy to you, because I, the LORD who sanctifies you, am holy.
verses.21:9: And if the daughter of any priest profanes herself by committing harlotry, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.
verses.21:10: Now the priest who is chief among his brethren, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the garments, shall not let the hair of his head hang loose, nor tear his garments.
verses.21:11: Neither shall he go near any dead body, nor defile himself for his father or for his mother.
verses.21:12: And he shall not depart from the sanctuary, nor profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is upon him: I am the LORD.
verses.21:13: Moreover, he shall take a wife in her virginity.
verses.21:14: A widow, or a divorced woman, or one who has been defiled, or a harlot—these he shall not marry; rather, he shall take a virgin of his own people as his wife.
verses.21:15: Thus he shall not profane his offspring among his people, for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.'"
verses.21:16: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.21:17: "Speak to Aaron, saying, 'No man of your offspring throughout their generations who has any blemish shall draw near to offer the bread of his God.
verses.21:18: For no man in whom there is a blemish shall draw near: a man who is blind, or lame, or has a disfigured face, or a limb too long,
verses.21:19: or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,
verses.21:20: or is a hunchback, or a dwarf, or has a clouded spot in his eye, or an itching disease, or scabs, or crushed testicles.
verses.21:21: No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall come near to present the fire offerings of the LORD; he has a blemish, so he shall not come near to present the bread of his God.
verses.21:22: He may eat the bread of his God, both from the most holy things and from the holy things;
verses.21:23: only he shall not come near the veil nor approach the altar, because he has a blemish, lest he profane My sanctuaries; for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'"
verses.21:24: Thus Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel.
verses.22:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:2: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they keep themselves separate from the holy things of the children of Israel, so that they do not profane My holy name in what they consecrate to Me: I am the LORD.
verses.22:3: Say to them, 'Throughout your generations, any man of all your offspring who draws near to the holy things which the children of Israel consecrate to the LORD while his uncleanness is upon him—that soul shall be cut off from My presence: I am the LORD.
verses.22:4: No man of the offspring of Aaron who is a leper or has a bodily discharge shall eat of the holy things until he is clean. And whoever touches anything defiled by the dead, or a man who has an emission of seed,
verses.22:5: or a man who touches any creeping thing by which he may be made unclean, or any person by whom he may be made unclean, whatever his uncleanness may be—
verses.22:6: the person who touches any such thing shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat from the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
verses.22:7: When the sun has set, he shall be clean; and afterward he may eat of the holy things, because it is his food.
verses.22:8: What dies of itself or is torn by beasts he shall not eat, lest he defile himself with it: I am the LORD.
verses.22:9: They shall therefore keep My charge, lest they incur sin because of it and die for it when they profane it: I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
verses.22:10: No outsider shall eat any holy thing; neither a guest residing with a priest nor a hired servant shall eat any holy thing.
verses.22:11: But if a priest purchases a person with his own money, that one may eat of it; and those born in his house may also eat of his food.
verses.22:12: If a priest's daughter marries an outsider, she shall not eat of the heave offering of the holy things.
verses.22:13: Yet if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, and has no offspring, and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat of her father's food; but no outsider shall eat of it.
verses.22:14: And if a man eats a holy thing unintentionally, he shall add one-fifth to it and repay the holy thing to the priest.
verses.22:15: And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel which they offer up to the LORD,
verses.22:16: nor cause them to bear the iniquity of guilt when they eat their holy things; for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'"
verses.22:17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:18: "Speak to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and declare to them, 'Any man of the house of Israel, or of the sojourners in Israel, who brings his offering for any of their vows or for any of their freewill offerings which they present to the LORD as a burnt offering,
verses.22:19: that it may be accepted on your behalf, it shall be a male without blemish, from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.
verses.22:20: Whatever has a blemish you shall not present, for it shall not be accepted on your behalf.
verses.22:21: And whoever presents a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD to fulfill a special vow, or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock—it must be without blemish to be accepted; no blemish at all shall be in it.
verses.22:22: Any animal that is blind, or fractured, or maimed, or has a running sore, or an itching disease, or scabs—these you shall not offer to the LORD, nor place any of them as a fire offering upon the altar to the LORD.
verses.22:23: An ox or a sheep that has a limb too long or too short you may present as a freewill offering, but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
verses.22:24: Any animal that is bruised, or crushed, or torn, or cut you shall not offer to the LORD, nor shall you do such things in your land.
verses.22:25: Neither from the hand of a foreigner shall you present any of these as the bread of your God, because their deformity is in them and a blemish is in them; they shall not be accepted for you.'"
verses.22:26: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:27: "When an ox, or a sheep, or a goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother; and from the eighth day onward it shall be accepted as a fire offering to the LORD.
verses.22:28: Whether an ox or a sheep, you shall not slaughter both it and its young on the same day.
verses.22:29: And when you offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, you shall offer it so that it may be accepted on your behalf.
verses.22:30: On that same day it shall be eaten; you shall leave none of it until the morning: I am the LORD.
verses.22:31: Therefore you shall keep My commandments and perform them: I am the LORD.
verses.22:32: And you shall not profane My holy name, but I will be hallowed in the midst of the children of Israel; I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
verses.22:33: who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God: I am the LORD."
verses.23:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:2: "Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: 'The appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations—these are My appointed times.
verses.23:3: Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation. You shall not do any work; it is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.
verses.23:4: These are the appointed times of the LORD, the holy convocations which you shall proclaim at their appointed times:
verses.23:5: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, is the Passover to the LORD.
verses.23:6: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the LORD; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.23:7: On the first day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall not do any laborious work.
verses.23:8: And you shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD for seven days. On the seventh day is a holy convocation; you shall not do any laborious work.'"
verses.23:9: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:10: "Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: 'When you enter the land which I am giving to you, and reap its harvest, then you shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest.
verses.23:11: He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD for your acceptance; on the day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.
verses.23:12: And on the day when you wave the sheaf, you shall offer a male lamb without blemish, a year old, as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.23:13: Its grain offering shall be two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering made by fire to the LORD for a soothing aroma; and its drink offering shall be of wine, a fourth of a hin.
verses.23:14: You shall eat neither bread, nor roasted grain, nor fresh grain until this very day, until you have brought the offering of your God; it shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.23:15: And you shall count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought the sheaf of the wave offering: seven complete Sabbaths they shall be.
verses.23:16: Until the day after the seventh Sabbath you shall count fifty days; then you shall present a new grain offering to the LORD.
verses.23:17: From your dwellings you shall bring two wave loaves made of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour; they shall be baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.
verses.23:18: And with the bread you shall present seven male lambs without blemish, a year old, one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the LORD, along with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering made by fire of a soothing aroma to the LORD.
verses.23:19: Then you shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two male lambs a year old as a sacrifice of peace offerings.
verses.23:20: And the priest shall wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before the LORD, together with the two lambs; they shall be holy to the LORD for the priest.
verses.23:21: And you shall make proclamation on this very day; there shall be a holy convocation for you. You shall not do any laborious work; it shall be a perpetual statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations.
verses.23:22: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corner of your field when you reap, nor shall you gather the gleaning of your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner. I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.23:23: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:24: "Speak to the children of Israel, saying: 'In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a solemn rest, a memorial of trumpet blasts, a holy convocation.
verses.23:25: You shall not do any laborious work, and you shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD.'"
verses.23:26: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:27: "Moreover, on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall afflict your souls, and present an offering made by fire to the LORD.
verses.23:28: And you shall not do any work on this very day, for it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
verses.23:29: For any person who is not afflicted on this very day shall be cut off from his people.
verses.23:30: And any person who does any work on this very day, that very person I will destroy from the midst of his people.
verses.23:31: You shall not do any work; it shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.23:32: It shall be to you a Sabbath of solemn rest, and you shall afflict your souls; on the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall observe your Sabbath."
verses.23:33: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:34: "Speak to the children of Israel, saying: 'On the fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the Feast of Booths for seven days to the LORD.
verses.23:35: On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall not do any laborious work.
verses.23:36: For seven days you shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall have a holy convocation, and you shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you shall not do any laborious work.
verses.23:37: These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to present an offering made by fire to the LORD—a burnt offering and a grain offering, a sacrifice and drink offerings, each on its own day—
verses.23:38: besides the Sabbaths of the LORD, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your freewill offerings which you give to the LORD.
verses.23:39: Moreover, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall celebrate the feast of the LORD for seven days; on the first day there shall be a solemn rest, and on the eighth day there shall be a solemn rest.
verses.23:40: And on the first day you shall take for yourselves the fruit of majestic trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook; and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
verses.23:41: You shall celebrate it as a feast to the LORD for seven days in the year. It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
verses.23:42: You shall dwell in booths for seven days; every native-born in Israel shall dwell in booths,
verses.23:43: that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.23:44: So Moses declared the appointed times of the LORD to the children of Israel.
verses.24:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:2: "Command the children of Israel that they bring to you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, to keep a lamp burning continually.
verses.24:3: Outside the veil of the Testimony, in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron shall keep it in order from evening until morning before the LORD continually; it shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
verses.24:4: He shall keep the lamps in order on the pure lampstand before the LORD continually.
verses.24:5: And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves with it; two tenths of an ephah shall be in each loaf.
verses.24:6: You shall set them in two rows, six in a row, upon the pure table before the LORD.
verses.24:7: And you shall put pure frankincense upon each row, that it may be with the bread as a memorial portion, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
verses.24:8: Every Sabbath day he shall set it in order before the LORD continually, taken from the children of Israel as an everlasting covenant.
verses.24:9: And it shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place; for it is most holy to him from the offerings made by fire to the LORD, as a perpetual due."
verses.24:10: Now the son of an Israelite woman, who was the son of an Egyptian man, went out among the children of Israel; and the son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought together in the camp.
verses.24:11: And the son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed; so they brought him to Moses. Now his mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
verses.24:12: And they put him in custody, that it might be declared clearly to them by the word of the LORD.
verses.24:13: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:14: "Bring the one who cursed outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
verses.24:15: And you shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: 'Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin.
verses.24:16: And whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall surely stone him. Both the sojourner and the native-born, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.
verses.24:17: And whoever strikes down any human life shall surely be put to death.
verses.24:18: And whoever strikes down the life of an animal shall make restitution for it, life for life.
verses.24:19: If a man causes an injury to his neighbor, just as he has done, so it shall be done to him:
verses.24:20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; just as he has caused an injury to a person, so it shall be inflicted on him.
verses.24:21: Whoever strikes down an animal shall make restitution for it, and whoever strikes down a man shall be put to death.
verses.24:22: You shall have one law; it shall be for the sojourner as well as for the native-born, for I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.24:23: Then Moses spoke to the children of Israel; and they brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. Thus the children of Israel did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.25:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
verses.25:2: "Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: 'When you enter the land which I am giving to you, then the land shall keep a sabbath to the LORD.
verses.25:3: Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard, and gather in its produce;
verses.25:4: but in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field, nor shall you prune your vineyard.
verses.25:5: What grows of its own accord from your harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your untrimmed vine you shall not gather; it shall be a year of solemn rest for the land.
verses.25:6: And the sabbath yield of the land shall be food for you: for you, for your manservant and your maidservant, and for your hired servant and your sojourner who dwell with you,
verses.25:7: and for your livestock and the wild beasts that are in your land; all its produce shall be for food.
verses.25:8: And you shall count for yourself seven sabbaths of years, seven years seven times; and the period of the seven sabbaths of years shall be to you forty-nine years.
verses.25:9: Then you shall cause the trumpet of loud blast to sound in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month; on the Day of Atonement you shall cause the trumpet to sound throughout all your land.
verses.25:10: And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty in the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you; and each of you shall return to his possession, and each of you shall return to his family.
verses.25:11: That fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee for you; you shall not sow, nor reap what grows of its own accord, nor gather from its untrimmed vines.
verses.25:12: For it is the Jubilee; it shall be holy to you; from the field you shall eat its produce.
verses.25:13: In this Year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his possession.
verses.25:14: And if you sell anything to your neighbor or buy from the hand of your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.
verses.25:15: According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor, and according to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.
verses.25:16: According to the multitude of the years you shall increase its purchase price, and according to the fewness of the years you shall diminish its purchase price; for it is the number of crops that he is selling to you.
verses.25:17: And you shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God; for I am the LORD your God.
verses.25:18: So you shall carry out My statutes, and keep My judgments and perform them; and you shall dwell in the land in safety.
verses.25:19: Then the land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat to the full, and dwell upon it in safety.
verses.25:20: And if you say, "What shall we eat in the seventh year? Behold, we shall not sow nor gather in our produce,"
verses.25:21: then I will command My blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth produce for three years.
verses.25:22: And you shall sow in the eighth year, and eat from the old produce; until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, you shall eat of the old supply.
verses.25:23: The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with Me.
verses.25:24: And throughout all the land of your possession, you shall grant redemption for the land.
verses.25:25: If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his possession, then his redeemer who is nearest to him shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.
verses.25:26: Or if a man has no redeemer, yet he himself prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it,
verses.25:27: then he shall reckon the years since its sale, and restore the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his possession.
verses.25:28: But if he does not have sufficient means to repay him, then what was sold shall remain in the hand of him who bought it until the Year of Jubilee; and in the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his possession.
verses.25:29: If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then he may redeem it until the completion of a full year from its sale; for a full year he shall have the right of redemption.
verses.25:30: But if it is not redeemed before a full year is completed, then the house that is in the city which has a wall shall be established in perpetuity to him who bought it, throughout his generations; it shall not be released in the Jubilee.
verses.25:31: However, the houses of villages which have no wall around them shall be reckoned as the fields of the country; they may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
verses.25:32: As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities of their possession, the Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption.
verses.25:33: And if one redeems property from the Levites, then the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall be released in the Jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.
verses.25:34: But the field of the pastureland of their cities shall not be sold, for it is their perpetual possession.
verses.25:35: And if your brother becomes poor and his hand falters with you, then you shall uphold him; like a stranger and a sojourner, he shall live with you.
verses.25:36: Do not take interest or increase from him, but fear your God, that your brother may live with you.
verses.25:37: You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor lend your food for profit.
verses.25:38: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
verses.25:39: And if your brother who is with you becomes poor and sells himself to you, you shall not compel him to do the work of a bondservant.
verses.25:40: As a hired servant and as a sojourner he shall be with you; he shall serve with you until the Year of Jubilee.
verses.25:41: Then he shall go out from you—he and his children with him—and shall return to his own family, and to the possession of his fathers he shall return.
verses.25:42: For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold as bondservants.
verses.25:43: You shall not rule over him with rigor, but you shall fear your God.
verses.25:44: And as for your male and female servants whom you may have—from the nations that are around you, from them you may buy male and female servants.
verses.25:45: Moreover, from the children of the sojourners who dwell among you, from them you may buy, and from their families who are with you, whom they have fathered in your land; and they shall become your possession.
verses.25:46: And you may bequeath them as an inheritance to your children after you, to inherit as a possession; you may hold them in service forever; but over your brethren, the children of Israel, you shall not rule over one another with rigor.
verses.25:47: Now if a stranger or sojourner with you becomes prosperous, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the stranger or sojourner with you, or to an offshoot of the family of a stranger,
verses.25:48: after he is sold he shall have the right of redemption; one of his brothers may redeem him,
verses.25:49: or his uncle or the son of his uncle may redeem him, or anyone of his near kin from his family may redeem him; or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
verses.25:50: Then he shall reckon with him who bought him from the year that he sold himself to him until the Year of Jubilee; and the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years, reckoned with him according to the days of a hired servant.
verses.25:51: If there are still many years remaining, in proportion to them he shall repay the price of his redemption from the money with which he was bought.
verses.25:52: And if only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, then he shall reckon with him; according to his years he shall repay the price of his redemption.
verses.25:53: As a servant hired year by year he shall be with him; he shall not rule over him with rigor in your sight.
verses.25:54: And if he is not redeemed by these means, then he shall be released in the Year of Jubilee—he and his children with him.
verses.25:55: For to Me the children of Israel are servants; they are My servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.26:1: You shall not make idols for yourselves, nor shall you erect for yourselves a carved image or a sacred pillar, nor shall you place a figured stone in your land to bow down before it; for I am the LORD your God.
verses.26:2: My Sabbaths you shall keep, and My sanctuary you shall revere; I am the LORD.
verses.26:3: If you walk in My statutes, and observe My commandments and perform them,
verses.26:4: then I will grant your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the field shall give their fruit.
verses.26:5: Threshing shall overtake the vintage for you, and the vintage shall overtake the sowing; you shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell securely in your land.
verses.26:6: I will grant peace in the land, and you shall lie down with none to make you afraid; I will remove fierce beasts from the land, and no sword shall pass through your land.
verses.26:7: You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.
verses.26:8: Five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
verses.26:9: I will turn toward you with favor, and make you fruitful and multiply you, and uphold My covenant with you.
verses.26:10: You shall eat the old harvest long stored, and clear out the old because of the new.
verses.26:11: I will set My dwelling place among you, and My soul shall not abhor you.
verses.26:12: I will walk in your midst, and I will be your God, and you shall be My people.
verses.26:13: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that you should not be their slaves; I broke the bars of your yoke and led you forth upright.
verses.26:14: But if you do not listen to Me, and do not perform all these commandments,
verses.26:15: and if you spurn My statutes, or if your soul abhors My judgments, so that you do not perform all My commandments, so as to break My covenant,
verses.26:16: then I also will do this to you: I will appoint sudden terror over you, wasting disease and burning fever that consume the eyes and cause the soul to languish; and you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.
verses.26:17: I will set My face against you, and you shall be struck down before your enemies; those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
verses.26:18: And if after all these things you still do not listen to Me, then I will chasten you yet seven times more for your sins.
verses.26:19: I will break the pride of your might; I will make your heavens like iron and your earth like bronze.
verses.26:20: Your strength shall be spent in vain; your land shall not yield its produce, nor shall the trees of the land give their fruit.
verses.26:21: And if you walk contrary to Me and are unwilling to listen to Me, then I will bring upon you sevenfold more plagues, according to your sins.
verses.26:22: I will send the wild beasts of the field among you, which shall bereave you of your children, cut off your livestock, and make you few in number; and your roads shall lie desolate.
verses.26:23: And if by these things you are not disciplined by Me, but walk contrary to Me,
verses.26:24: then I also will walk contrary to you, and I Myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:25: I will bring upon you a sword that shall execute the vengeance of the covenant; and when you gather within your cities, I will send pestilence into your midst, and you shall be given into the hand of the enemy.
verses.26:26: When I break your staff of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall return your bread by weight; and you shall eat, yet not be satisfied.
verses.26:27: And if in spite of this you do not listen to Me, but walk contrary to Me,
verses.26:28: then I will walk contrary to you in fury, and I Myself will chasten you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:29: You shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you shall eat.
verses.26:30: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and cast your carcasses upon the carcasses of your idols; and My soul shall abhor you.
verses.26:31: I will lay your cities waste and bring your sanctuaries to desolation, and I will not smell the fragrance of your soothing aromas.
verses.26:32: I Myself will make the land desolate, so that your enemies who dwell in it shall be appalled at it.
verses.26:33: And you I will scatter among the nations, and I will unsheathe a sword after you; your land shall become a desolation, and your cities shall be a waste.
verses.26:34: Then the land shall enjoy its sabbaths all the days of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land shall rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
verses.26:35: All the days of its desolation it shall have rest, the rest that it did not have during your sabbaths when you dwelt upon it.
verses.26:36: And as for those of you who are left, I will send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; the sound of a driven leaf shall pursue them, and they shall flee as one flees from the sword, and fall though no one pursues.
verses.26:37: They shall stumble over one another as if before a sword, when no one pursues; and you shall have no power to stand before your enemies.
verses.26:38: You shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall devour you.
verses.26:39: And those of you who are left shall waste away in their iniquity in the lands of your enemies; and also because of the iniquities of their fathers with them they shall waste away.
verses.26:40: But if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, in their unfaithfulness with which they acted unfaithfully against Me, and also that they walked contrary to Me,
verses.26:41: so that I also walked contrary to them and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled, and then they make amends for their iniquity,
verses.26:42: then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham I will remember; and the land I will remember.
verses.26:43: For the land shall be forsaken by them, and shall enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them; and they shall make amends for their iniquity, because, even because they spurned My judgments and their soul abhorred My statutes.
verses.26:44: Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not spurn them, nor will I abhor them so as to destroy them utterly and break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.
verses.26:45: But for their sake I will remember the covenant of their forefathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God; I am the LORD.
verses.26:46: These are the statutes and judgments and laws which the LORD established between Himself and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
verses.27:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.27:2: "Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, 'When a man makes a special vow of persons to the LORD according to your valuation,
verses.27:3: then your valuation of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old—your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
verses.27:4: And if it is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
verses.27:5: And if from five years old up to twenty years old, then your valuation of the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
verses.27:6: And if from one month old up to five years old, then your valuation of the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female your valuation shall be three shekels of silver.
verses.27:7: And if from sixty years old and upward, if a male, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
verses.27:8: But if he is too poor for your valuation, then he shall present him before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to the means of him who made the vow, the priest shall value him.
verses.27:9: And if it is an animal from which men bring an offering to the LORD, whatever one gives of such to the LORD shall be holy.
verses.27:10: He shall not substitute for it nor exchange it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good; and if he exchanges animal for animal at all, then both it and its substitute shall be holy.
verses.27:11: And if it is any unclean animal, from which men do not bring an offering to the LORD, then he shall present the animal before the priest.
verses.27:12: And the priest shall value it, whether it is good or bad; according to your valuation, O priest, so it shall be.
verses.27:13: But if he will indeed redeem it, then he shall add one-fifth to your valuation.
verses.27:14: And when a man consecrates his house to be holy to the LORD, then the priest shall value it, whether it is good or bad; as the priest values it, so it shall stand.
verses.27:15: And if he who consecrated it redeems his house, then he shall add one-fifth of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.
verses.27:16: And if a man consecrates to the LORD part of a field of his possession, then your valuation shall be according to its seed: a homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver.
verses.27:17: If he consecrates his field from the Year of Jubilee, according to your valuation it shall stand.
verses.27:18: But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall reckon to him the money according to the years that remain until the Year of Jubilee, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation.
verses.27:19: And if he who consecrated the field will indeed redeem it, then he shall add one-fifth of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be confirmed to him.
verses.27:20: But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore.
verses.27:21: Rather, when the field is released in the Jubilee, it shall be holy to the LORD, as a devoted field; it shall be the possession of the priest.
verses.27:22: And if he consecrates to the LORD a field of his purchase, which is not part of the field of his possession,
verses.27:23: then the priest shall reckon to him the amount of the valuation up to the Year of Jubilee, and he shall give the valuation on that day, as a holy thing to the LORD.
verses.27:24: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to him from whom he bought it, to him to whom the possession of the land belongs.
verses.27:25: And every valuation of yours shall be according to the shekel of the sanctuary; the shekel shall be twenty gerahs.
verses.27:26: However, a firstborn of the animals, which as a firstborn belongs to the LORD, no man shall consecrate it; whether it is an ox or a sheep, it belongs to the LORD.
verses.27:27: And if it is among the unclean animals, then he shall ransom it according to your valuation, and shall add its fifth part to it; or if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.
verses.27:28: Nevertheless, no devoted thing that a man devotes to the LORD of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of the field of his possession, shall be sold or redeemed; every devoted thing is most holy to the LORD.
verses.27:29: No one devoted, who is devoted from among men, shall be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death.
verses.27:30: And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the tree, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
verses.27:31: And if a man will indeed redeem any of his tithe, he shall add its fifth part to it.
verses.27:32: And concerning every tithe of the herd and of the flock, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth one shall be holy to the LORD.
verses.27:33: He shall not examine whether it is good or bad, nor shall he exchange it; and if he exchanges it at all, then both it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'"
verses.27:34: These are the commandments which the LORD commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.

notes.1:3: The Hebrew phrase rendered for his acceptance may alternatively be translated of his own free will; the sense of acceptance corresponds closely to the verb accepted in verse four.
notes.1:5: The Hebrew verb rendered dash denotes tossing or throwing blood from a basin against the sides of the altar, distinct from sprinkling with the finger.
notes.1:9: The Hebrew verb rendered burn literally means to turn into smoke, used specifically for burning sacrificial portions upon the altar.
notes.1:16: The Hebrew term rendered feathers traditionally denotes plumage, though some ancient versions and interpreters understand it as the contents or filth of the crop.
notes.2:2: The memorial portion is the representative token share of the grain offering burned on the altar to bring the worshiper into remembrance before the LORD.
notes.2:11: The Hebrew word for honey includes both bee honey and sweet fruit syrups, such as date syrup, which were subject to fermentation.
notes.2:13: The salt of the covenant reflects salt as an ancient emblem of permanence, purity, and an enduring covenant bond.
notes.3:1: Peace offerings, from a Hebrew root denoting wholeness and well-being, were fellowship sacrifices whose meat was shared between the altar, the priests, and the worshiper.
notes.3:9: Broad-tailed sheep common in the ancient Near East have a heavy, fatty tail considered a choice portion reserved for the altar.
notes.3:11: The Hebrew word literally meaning bread or food is used figuratively for the choice sacrificial portions presented to the LORD upon the altar.
notes.4:3: The phrase "anointed priest" translates the Hebrew hakohen hamashiach, referring specifically to the high priest consecrated with the sacred anointing oil.
notes.4:10: "Offer them up in smoke" translates the Hebrew verb hiqtir, denoting altar burning as aromatic smoke, distinct from saraf ("burn" in 4:12 and 4:21), used for consuming the remainder outside the camp.
notes.4:22: The opening "When" translates the Hebrew relative particle asher, used here with conditional force in place of the usual im ("if") to introduce the case of a ruler (nasi).
notes.4:27: "The people of the land" translates the Hebrew am ha-arets, referring here to ordinary Israelite laypersons as distinct from the high priest, the full assembly, and a ruler.
notes.5:1: "The voice of a solemn adjuration" translates the Hebrew qol alah, a public imprecatory oath pronounced to summon anyone with knowledge of a wrongdoing to testify.
notes.5:6: "Guilt offering" translates the Hebrew asham (also rendered "trespass offering"), which in verses 6 and 7 refers to a reparation penalty brought as a sin offering, while verses 15 through 25 prescribe the distinct ram of the guilt offering.
notes.5:20: In the Masoretic Hebrew text, Leviticus 5:20 through 5:26 concludes chapter 5; many English versions number these seven verses as Leviticus 6:1 through 6:7.
notes.5:21: "A pledge placed in his hand" translates the Hebrew tesumet yad (literally "a placing of the hand"), denoting money, security, or property entrusted to another in a business or personal agreement.
notes.6:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew text, chapter six begins here, whereas most English translations number verses 6:1 through 6:23 as 6:8 through 6:30.
notes.6:2: The Hebrew term mokedah, translated hearth, refers to the burning surface of the altar and is traditionally written in Masoretic manuscripts with a diminutive letter mem.
notes.6:14: The Hebrew word tuphine, translated baked pieces, occurs only here in the Old Testament and denotes baked or fried portions of the high priest's daily grain offering.
notes.6:19: The Hebrew verb form hamechatte, translated offers it for sin, is a ritual Piel form denoting the priest who performs the purification or sin offering.
notes.7:1: The Hebrew noun asham, translated guilt offering and traditionally also rendered trespass offering, denotes a reparation sacrifice for sacred or interpersonal offenses.
notes.7:18: The Hebrew term piggul, translated abomination, is a technical priestly designation for sacrificial meat rendered ritually foul and unacceptable.
notes.7:24: Hebrew distinguishes nevelah, an animal that dies of itself, from terephah, an animal torn by wild beasts; while their fat could be put to ordinary non-dietary uses, eating it remained strictly forbidden.
notes.7:35: The Hebrew word mishchah, translated consecrated portion, carries the sense of an anointing share or allotted portion assigned to Aaron and his sons upon their ordination.
notes.8:16: Hebrew distinguishes between hiqtir, used here for turning sacrificial portions into smoke upon the altar, and saraf in verse 17, used for burning the remainder with fire outside the camp.
notes.8:31: The Masoretic vocalization reads the active form tsivviti, meaning I have commanded, whereas the parallel expression in verse 35 is pointed passively as tsuvveti, meaning I have been commanded.
notes.8:33: Literally, for seven days one will fill your hand; filling the hand is the standard Hebrew idiom for ordaining or installing priests into office, corresponding to the noun ordination (milluim).
notes.9:7: The Masoretic Hebrew text explicitly reads for yourself and for the people, translated directly without harmonizing to ancient versions that read for your household.
notes.9:19: Hebrew introduces the fat portions as an anticipatory clause resumed by the verb in verse 20; the covering fat refers to the layer of fat covering the entrails.
notes.9:22: The consonantal text spells yadav defectively without a yod, resembling the singular his hand, while the Masoretic vocalization reads the plural his hands.
notes.10:1: Hebrew 'esh zarah ('strange fire') denotes unauthorized or profane fire presented contrary to the divine prescription.
notes.10:6: Letting the hair hang loose and tearing garments were customary mourning rites forbidden to consecrated priests bearing the LORD's anointing oil.
notes.10:16: Hebrew darosh darash ('diligently inquired') employs the infinitive absolute for emphasis; Masoretic tradition marks these words as the midpoint of the Torah by word count.
notes.11:5: The Hebrew source text lists the hare ('arnevet) in verse 5 and the rock badger (shaphan, rock hyrax) in verse 6; both perform chewing motions resembling rumination though they lack divided hooves.
notes.11:13: Several Hebrew bird names in verses 13-19 and small-creature names in verses 29-30 have uncertain exact zoological identifications and are rendered according to standard lexicographical consensus.
notes.11:21: Translated according to the Masoretic Qere lo ('that have'); the Ketiv reads lo' ('not'), a common homophonous orthographic variant in Hebrew manuscripts.
notes.11:43: The Hebrew text pairs the Hithpael and Niphal stems of tame' ('make yourselves unclean' and 'be defiled') to underscore the spiritual gravity of maintaining ritual purity.
notes.12:2: The Hebrew verb tazria literally means "yields seed" and idiomatically denotes conceiving. The phrase niddat devotah pairs the term for ritual separation with that for monthly infirmity.
notes.12:4: The Masoretic Text reads "blood of purification" without a possessive suffix (here and in verse 5), distinguishing it from "days of her purification" at the end of this verse and in verse 6.
notes.12:7: Literally "from the fountain of her blood," employing the Hebrew plural form for blood to denote the postpartum discharge.
notes.12:8: Literally "if her hand does not find sufficiency for a lamb," an idiomatic expression for lacking the financial means to provide a lamb.
notes.13:2: Hebrew tsara'at, traditionally rendered "leprosy," encompasses a range of scaly or disfiguring skin afflictions as well as contaminating growths on garments and walls (cf. 13:47; 14:34), rather than solely modern Hansen's disease.
notes.13:4: Literally "confine the plague," using the affliction by metonymy for the afflicted person (similarly in verses 12, 13, and 17).
notes.13:5: The Hebrew idiom "stood in his eyes" denotes that the affliction remained unchanged in appearance as observed by the priest.
notes.13:30: Hebrew neteq denotes a scaly eruption of the scalp or beard affecting the hair, traditionally rendered "scall" or "scale."
notes.13:39: Hebrew bohaq refers to a benign, dull white skin eruption or discoloration that does not render a person ceremonially unclean.
notes.13:45: Tearing the garments, leaving the hair unkempt, and covering the upper lip were traditional Israelite signs of mourning (cf. Leviticus 10:6; Ezekiel 24:17), marking the afflicted person's separation from the community.
notes.13:55: Literally "on its back baldness or on its front baldness," reusing the terms from verses 42-43 metaphorically for the worn back or front side of the fabric.
notes.14:2: The Hebrew term rendered leprosy encompasses a range of serious skin afflictions as well as fungal mildew or mold in garments and houses.
notes.14:5: Literally living water, referring to fresh running water drawn from a spring or flowing stream rather than standing water.
notes.14:10: A tenth of an ephah was a dry measure of roughly two quarts, and a log was a liquid measure of approximately one-third of a quart.
notes.14:37: The Hebrew word for depressions occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes sunken or hollow streaks in the plastered wall.
notes.14:57: Literally in the day of the unclean and in the day of the clean.
notes.15:2: Hebrew basar, translated flesh, is used throughout this chapter for the body and euphemistically for the genital organ.
notes.15:13: Running water renders Hebrew mayim chayyim, literally living water, referring to fresh spring or flowing water.
notes.15:31: Tabernacle renders Hebrew mishkan, dwelling place, distinguishing it from tent of meeting, Hebrew ohel moed, in verses fourteen and twenty-nine.
notes.16:2: Mercy seat is the traditional liturgical rendering of Hebrew kapporet, the golden atonement cover placed upon the ark of the Testimony.
notes.16:8: Hebrew Azazel, traditionally rendered scapegoat, is of debated etymology and is understood either as a goat sent away or as a designation for a remote wilderness place.
notes.16:21: An appointed man translates Hebrew ish itti, literally a timely man, signifying one designated and ready for the task.
notes.16:22: A solitary land renders Hebrew erets gezerah, literally a land cut off, referring to an uninhabited region in the wilderness.
notes.16:29: Afflict your souls is the traditional Hebrew idiom for humble self-denial, especially fasting, observed on the Day of Atonement.
notes.17:4: Hebrew literally reads "blood shall be reckoned to that man," an idiom denoting bloodguilt incurred by unauthorized slaughter.
notes.17:7: Hebrew se'irim literally means "hairy ones" or "goats," referring to goat-shaped demon idols worshipped in the open field.
notes.17:11: Hebrew nephesh ("life" or "soul") occurs three times in this verse; the final phrase, literally "by the life," indicates that blood makes atonement because it bears the life of the sacrifice.
notes.17:14: Hebrew literally reads "its blood is in its life," expressing the complete identification between the blood and the life of every living creature.
notes.18:6: Hebrew literally reads "flesh of his flesh," an idiom denoting close blood relatives.
notes.18:7: The phrase "uncover nakedness" is a standard Hebrew idiom throughout this chapter for unlawful sexual relations.
notes.18:21: Hebrew "to pass over to Molech" is an idiom for the pagan rite of child sacrifice by fire.
notes.18:23: Hebrew tebel denotes a grave perversion or unnatural violation of the created order.
notes.19:5: The Hebrew phrase rendered "so that you may be accepted" denotes offering the peace sacrifice in the prescribed manner to secure divine favor, though some render it "of your own free will."
notes.19:16: "Stand against the blood of your neighbor" is a Hebrew idiom forbidding both plotting against another's life and standing idly by when his life is in danger.
notes.19:20: The Hebrew noun rendered "inquiry" occurs only here in Scripture and refers to a formal judicial investigation or penalty short of the death sentence.
notes.19:36: An "ephah" was a dry measure of roughly three-fifths of a bushel, and a "hin" was a liquid measure of about one gallon.
notes.20:2: "Molech" was an ancient Near Eastern deity linked with child sacrifice, strictly forbidden under penalty of death in Israel.
notes.20:9: "His blood shall be upon him" is a legal declaration indicating that the offender alone bears guilt for his execution.
notes.20:17: The Hebrew term rendered "disgrace" is a rare homonym of the common word for "lovingkindness," signifying shameful reproach.
notes.20:25: The Hebrew orders the pairs chiastically—clean beast to unclean, then unclean bird to clean—highlighting the call to maintain strict ritual separation.
notes.21:4: The Hebrew word baal here can mean either a husband (forbidding defilement for relatives by marriage) or a chief man and leader among his people.
notes.21:5: Ketiv/qere variant: the written consonantal text (ketiv) has an extra initial yod before the noun, whereas the read form (qere) gives the standard noun for a bald patch or baldness, translated here.
notes.21:10: Consecrated is literally whose hand has been filled; leaving the hair unbound and tearing garments were customary signs of mourning forbidden to the high priest.
notes.21:20: Several of the Hebrew terms for physical blemishes and skin afflictions in this verse are rare, so their exact medical equivalents remain somewhat uncertain.
notes.22:2: Keep themselves separate translates a Hebrew verb meaning to abstain or hold aloof, directing the priests to refrain from handling or eating sacred offerings while ritually unclean.
notes.22:10: Outsider (Hebrew zar) refers here not necessarily to a foreigner, but to any unauthorized person outside the priestly household.
notes.22:24: The four Hebrew participles—bruised, crushed, torn, and cut—refer to forms of castration or injury to an animal's reproductive organs, forbidden both in sacrifices and as a practice within Israel.
notes.22:27: With its mother is literally under its mother, referring to the seven-day period in which the newborn animal remains nursing with its mother before becoming acceptable for sacrifice.
notes.23:2: Hebrew mo'adim means appointed times or appointed seasons, a broader category encompassing the weekly Sabbath, the Day of Atonement, and the annual pilgrim feasts.
notes.23:5: Literally between the two evenings, referring to the twilight period between late afternoon or sunset and full darkness.
notes.23:13: Hebrew literally reads two tenths, understood as tenths of an ephah; soothing aroma reflects Hebrew reach nichoach, signifying an offering acceptable and pleasing to the LORD.
notes.23:15: Literally seven complete Sabbaths, denoting seven full weeks leading to the fiftieth day, the Feast of Weeks.
notes.23:27: Afflict your souls is a Hebrew idiom for humble self-denial, especially fasting, practiced on the Day of Atonement.
notes.23:34: Hebrew Sukkot, traditionally also called the Feast of Tabernacles, commemorating the temporary shelters in which Israel dwelt during the wilderness journey.
notes.24:5: The twelve loaves of the bread of the Presence correspond to the twelve tribes of Israel, set continually before the LORD on the golden table.
notes.24:11: The Name (Hebrew ha-Shem) refers to the sacred covenant name of the LORD; the verb rendered blasphemed carries the sense of piercing or uttering profanely.
notes.24:19: This statute of proportional restitution and justice limits retaliation to the measure of the injury and applies equally to both native-born Israelites and sojourners.
notes.25:5: The Hebrew term for untrimmed vine literally denotes a consecrated or untended vine, employing the same root used for the uncut hair of a Nazirite.
notes.25:10: The word Jubilee derives from the Hebrew yovel, denoting the ram's horn blown to proclaim the fiftieth year of liberty and restoration.
notes.25:30: Following the Qere reading ("which has a wall"), which accords with verse 29; the Ketiv reads the homophonous negative particle ("not").
notes.25:33: The Masoretic Hebrew states concisely that when Levitical house property is acquired or redeemed from the Levites, it still reverts in the Jubilee, since these houses constitute their sole hereditary possession in Israel.
notes.26:1: The phrase figured stone translates a Hebrew expression for a carved or engraved stone set in place for idolatrous prostration.
notes.26:21: The idiom walk contrary to Me renders a Hebrew term found only in this chapter, denoting stubborn opposition, hostility, or willful disregard of God.
notes.26:34: The Hebrew verb rendered enjoy also carries the legal sense of paying off or making restitution, linking the land's forced sabbatical rest with the people making amends for their iniquity in verses 41 and 43.
notes.26:42: The patriarchs are named in reverse chronological order, tracing the covenant back to its origin; in the Masoretic text the name Jacob is written here in its rare full spelling.
notes.27:2: The Hebrew expression for your valuation carries a fossilized second-person singular suffix and functions throughout this chapter as a technical legal term for the fixed priestly assessment scale.
notes.27:16: A homer was a large dry measure of roughly six bushels; agricultural land was assessed by the quantity of barley seed needed to sow it.
notes.27:23: Here the Masoretic text attaches the definite article to the suffixed form for your valuation, confirming its idiomatic use as a fixed noun meaning the valuation.
notes.27:25: The shekel of the sanctuary was the standard temple weight of silver, fixed at twenty gerahs.
notes.27:28: A devoted thing translates Hebrew cherem, denoting persons, animals, or property irrevocably dedicated to the LORD that could never be sold or redeemed.
